paragraphs.text: Let us fear therefore, lest haply, a promise being left of entering into his rest, any one of you should seem to have come short of it.
paragraphs.original: Φοβηθῶμεν οὖν μήποτε καταλειπομένης ἐπαγγελίας εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ δοκῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ὑστερηκέναι·
paragraphs.translit: Phobēthōmen oun mēpote kataleipomenēs epangelias eiselthein eis tēn katapausin autou dokē tis ex hymōn hysterēkenai·

paragraphs.text: For indeed we have had good tidings preached unto us, even as also they: but the word of hearing did not profit them, because it was not united by faith with them that heard.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι, ἀλλʼ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους, μὴ συγκεκερασμένους τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar esmen euēngelismenoi kathaper kakeinoi, allʼ ouk ōphelēsen ho logos tēs akoēs ekeinous, mē synkekerasmenous tē pistei tois akousasin.

paragraphs.text: For we who have believed do enter into that rest; even as he hath said, As I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest:     although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
paragraphs.original: εἰσερχόμεθα γὰρ εἰς κατάπαυσιν οἱ πιστεύσαντες, καθὼς εἴρηκεν· Ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου, Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου, καίτοι τῶν ἔργων ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου γενηθέντων,
paragraphs.translit: eiserchometha gar eis katapausin hoi pisteusantes, kathōs eirēken· Hōs ōmosa en tē orgē mou, Ei eiseleusontai eis tēn katapausin mou, kaitoi tōn ergōn apo katabolēs kosmou genēthentōn,

paragraphs.text: For he hath said somewhere of the seventh [day] on this wise, And God rested on the seventh day from all his works;
paragraphs.original: εἴρηκεν γάρ που περὶ τῆς ἑβδόμης οὕτως· Καὶ κατέπαυσεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: eirēken gar pou peri tēs hebdomēs houtōs· Kai katepausen ho theos en tē hēmera tē hebdomē apo pantōn tōn ergōn autou,

paragraphs.text: and in this [place] again, They shall not enter into my rest.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ πάλιν· Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai en toutō palin· Ei eiseleusontai eis tēn katapausin mou.

paragraphs.text: Seeing therefore it remaineth that some should enter thereinto, and they to whom the good tidings were before preached failed to enter in because of disobedience,
paragraphs.original: ἐπεὶ οὖν ἀπολείπεται τινὰς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς αὐτήν, καὶ οἱ πρότερον εὐαγγελισθέντες οὐκ εἰσῆλθον διʼ ἀπείθειαν,
paragraphs.translit: epei oun apoleipetai tinas eiselthein eis autēn, kai hoi proteron euangelisthentes ouk eisēlthon diʼ apeitheian,

paragraphs.text: he again defineth a certain day, To-day, saying in David so long a time afterward (even as hath been said before), To-day if ye shall hear his voice, Harden not your hearts.
paragraphs.original: πάλιν τινὰ ὁρίζει ἡμέραν, Σήμερον, ἐν Δαυὶδ λέγων μετὰ τοσοῦτον χρόνον, καθὼς προείρηται, Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: palin tina horizei hēmeran, Sēmeron, en Dauid legōn meta tosouton chronon, kathōs proeirētai, Sēmeron ean tēs phōnēs autou akousēte, mē sklērynēte tas kardias hymōn·

paragraphs.text: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ αὐτοὺς Ἰησοῦς κατέπαυσεν, οὐκ ἂν περὶ ἄλλης ἐλάλει μετὰ ταῦτα ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar autous Iēsous katepausen, ouk an peri allēs elalei meta tauta hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: There remaineth therefore a sabbath rest for the people of God.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμὸς τῷ λαῷ τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ara apoleipetai sabbatismos tō laō tou theou·

paragraphs.text: For he that is entered into his rest hath himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar eiselthōn eis tēn katapausin autou kai autos katepausen apo tōn ergōn autou hōsper apo tōn idiōn ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Let us therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, that no man fall after the same example of disobedience.
paragraphs.original: σπουδάσωμεν οὖν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν κατάπαυσιν, ἵνα μὴ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ τις ὑποδείγματι πέσῃ τῆς ἀπειθείας.
paragraphs.translit: spoudasōmen oun eiselthein eis ekeinēn tēn katapausin, hina mē en tō autō tis hypodeigmati pesē tēs apeitheias.

paragraphs.text: For the word of God is living, and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, and piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and quick to discern the thoughts and intents of the heart.
paragraphs.original: Ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐνεργὴς καὶ τομώτερος ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον καὶ διϊκνούμενος ἄχρι μερισμοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ πνεύματος, ἁρμῶν τε καὶ μυελῶν, καὶ κριτικὸς ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας·
paragraphs.translit: Zōn gar ho logos tou theou kai energēs kai tomōteros hyper pasan machairan distomon kai diiknoumenos achri merismou psychēs kai pneumatos, harmōn te kai myelōn, kai kritikos enthymēseōn kai ennoiōn kardias·

paragraphs.text: And there is no creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν κτίσις ἀφανὴς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, πάντα δὲ γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ, πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk estin ktisis aphanēs enōpion autou, panta de gymna kai tetrachēlismena tois ophthalmois autou, pros hon hēmin ho logos.

paragraphs.text: Having then a great high priest, who hath passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession.
paragraphs.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν ἀρχιερέα μέγαν διεληλυθότα τοὺς οὐρανούς, Ἰησοῦν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, κρατῶμεν τῆς ὁμολογίας·
paragraphs.translit: Echontes oun archierea megan dielēlythota tous ouranous, Iēsoun ton hyion tou theou, kratōmen tēs homologias·

paragraphs.text: For we have not a high priest that cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but one that hath been in all points tempted like as [we are, yet] without sin.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα μὴ δυνάμενον συμπαθῆσαι ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ἡμῶν, πεπειρασμένον δὲ κατὰ πάντα καθʼ ὁμοιότητα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar echomen archierea mē dynamenon sympathēsai tais astheneiais hēmōn, pepeirasmenon de kata panta kathʼ homoiotēta chōris hamartias.

paragraphs.text: Let us therefore draw near with boldness unto the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace to help [us] in time of need.
paragraphs.original: προσερχώμεθα οὖν μετὰ παρρησίας τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος, ἵνα λάβωμεν ἔλεος καὶ χάριν εὕρωμεν εἰς εὔκαιρον βοήθειαν.
paragraphs.translit: proserchōmetha oun meta parrēsias tō thronō tēs charitos, hina labōmen eleos kai charin heurōmen eis eukairon boētheian.
